test_title: PYST 18: Selection Post (Matric Level) - General Intelligence (Held On 24 Jun 2024 Shift 4)
subject: reasoning
question:
Three statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

1) All cobblers are masons.

2) No mason is an electrician.

3) Some electricians are plumbers.

**Conclusions:**

I. All plumbers can never be masons.

II. At least some electricians are cobblers.

options.text: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows.
Both Conclusions I and II follow.

solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/93cb1008d25b387aa9d82f37374ec5084aa08f83e4e4b4275b208b8b5fcbf5b6.png] 

Conclusions:

I. All plumbers can never be masons → **F**ollow (As all cobblers are masons, no mason is an electrician and some electricians are plumbers. As whole cobblers comes in masons which cannot be electrician which have some part is common with plumbers, therefore all plumbers can never be masons is true.)

II. At least some electricians are cobblers → Does not follow (As all cobblers are masons and no mason is an electrician. As whole cobblers comes in masons which cannot be electricians, therefore it is false.)

∴ Here, Only conclusion I follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3"
